subject: Availability shift notice and immediate customer ops guidance
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@megacorp.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Service errors in US/EU - immediate assistance required

Hi Laura / Redwood team,

We're seeing a spike of 503s and long tail latencies for inference in our us-east and eu-west regions starting ~08:00 PDT. Error rate has jumped from ~0.2% to 4.8% and some production routes have timed out. Our users are reporting failures across both web and mobile.

Can you confirm whether any maintenance or regional incidents are underway on your side? If you have a recommended mitigation (temporary reroute or header change), we need to apply it ASAP — we have a sales-critical demo in 30 minutes.

Attached a short snippet of request/response headers and a few example traces: error_snippet.txt

Thanks,
Dana
Customer Success / MegaCorp Systems

---
(Please note I'm sending from ops — CC'd Ravi Patel from our platform team.)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@megacorp.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service errors in US/EU - immediate assistance required

Hi Dana — thanks for the quick heads-up and the trace snippets. We're seeing a correlated capacity pressure event affecting two cloud zones that service us-east and eu-west for your account.

Immediate mitigation we recommend (low-risk, takes <5 minutes):
- Point traffic to apac-1 as a temporary fallback by adding header X-Redwood-Region: apac-1 on requests OR
- Update your load balancer to prefer apac endpoints for the next 45 minutes while we stabilize.

We prepared a short one-page steps doc for ops: redwood_quick_reroute_steps.pdf (attached). Key notes: TTL for DNS changes shouldn't be more than 60s; use sticky-session cookie preservation described on page 1 to keep user sessions intact.

I'll kick off a canary to validate correctness and monitor error rate. We'll keep you posted every 10 minutes. If you want us to perform the header swap on your behalf, confirm and we'll proceed under the existing runbook.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-18T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service errors in US/EU - immediate assistance required

Thanks Laura — I started the canary run (10% traffic to apac-1) and am seeing error rates drop for the canary group. Summary so far:
- Canary (apac-1): error rate down to 0.5% after 3 minutes
- Remaining (us/eu): error rate still ~4.5%

Action items for immediate ops (my notes attached as canary_checklist.csv):
1) Execute header-based routing for critical routes: X-Redwood-Region: apac-1 (we can toggle back once rates normalize)
2) Raise TTL to 5s for the temporary route to avoid long cache durations for clients we can't control
3) If any route requires session affinity, follow the sticky-cookie guidance in the PDF

Jonas / Vanessa — can you prepare the escalation blurb for engineering and start collecting instance-level CPU/KV cache stats for the affected zones? We need: kernel panic logs, scheduler traces, and model-serving stall traces.

I'll send a customer-facing update once we confirm the broader traffic shift.

— Stephanie
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@megacorp.com>, ravi.patel@orangecloud.io (Ravi Patel)
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: availability shift resolved — next steps and post-incident items

Hi Dana / Ravi —

Thanks again for your patience while we triaged the event. Quick summary of what happened and what we need from you to close the loop: 

What we observed
- Root cause: transient scheduler contention combined with a degraded kernel thread pool on two underlying compute clusters serving us-east and eu-west. This caused KV cache stalls and request queueing that increased tail latency and 503s.
- Mitigation applied: temporary traffic shift to apac-1 (header-based) and small autoscaling bump; error rates returned to baseline within ~18 minutes after shift.

What Redwood did
- Coordinated a canary shift and validated with your SREs (see timeline in attached PDF).
- Performed targeted autoscale and reclaimed stuck kernel threads on the affected clusters.
- Opened an internal incident INC-2026-8421 for longer-term remediation.

What we need from you
1) Please upload a short set of end-to-end traces covering the 07:50–08:20 PDT window to the support ticket: https://redwood-support.example.com/tickets/INC-2026-8421
2) Confirm whether we should schedule a 30-minute joint postmortem next week (proposed window: Tue 10/26, 09:00–09:30 PDT).

Attachments included: redwood_quick_reroute_steps.pdf (ops steps we used), canary_checklist.csv (canary verification), error_snippet.txt (your original traces).

We'll follow up with a longer root-cause analysis with metrics and remediation timelines in the ticket. If you want us to implement persistent multi-region failover (automated routing policy) for MegaCorp, we can scope costs and a timeline.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
